title: The code that runs, in order

steps.title: Four stages, the files that matter in each
steps.body: Each coloured block is one stage with the repository it lives in. The rows are the source files worth opening to understand or change that stage; all paths are relative to the checkouts under `build/src/`.

steps.title: BL2: find the FIP, start the memory
steps.body: `bl2_io_storage.c` finds the FIP partition. `bl2_plat_setup.c` calls `stm32mp1_ddr_probe()` and loads the images; `plat_bl2_mem_params_desc.c` and the `fw-config` device tree say where each goes. The DDR3 driver itself is `drivers/st/ddr/stm32mp1_ddr.c`.

steps.title: OP-TEE: configuration decides what it is
steps.body: `conf.mk` fixes the secure RAM at `0xde000000`, turns the pager on and enables the SCMI message server (`CFG_SCMI_MSG_DRIVERS`). `main.c` is the platform start-up and prints the platform banner.

steps.title: The monitor is OP-TEE
steps.body: `sm_smc_entry()` is the handler for every `smc` from the normal world. On the 64-bit board this job belongs to BL31; here there is none.

steps.title: The SCMI server's tables
steps.body: This file lists the clocks, reset domains and voltage domains the server answers for. The STPMIC1 rails (`buck4` = `v3v3`, which powers the SD card) are rows in it.

steps.title: U-Boot: from boot device to bootz
steps.body: `stm32mp1/cpu.c` sets `boot_device` and `boot_instance`, `stm32mp15_st_common.h` defines `bootcmd_stm32mp`, `config_distro_bootcmd.h` scans for `extlinux.conf`, `sysboot.c` parses it and `bootz.c` starts the kernel.

steps.title: U-Boot is an SCMI client too
steps.body: U-Boot also asks OP-TEE for clocks and regulators (`CONFIG_SCMI_FIRMWARE` in `stm32mp15_defconfig`), which is why its device tree is the SCMI variant.

steps.title: Linux: the SCMI side of the device tree and the drivers
steps.body: `stm32mp15-scmi.dtsi` declares the `scmi` node and its protocols, `transports/optee.c` turns each message into a call into OP-TEE, and `scmi-regulator.c` is what switches the SD card's supply. `mmci.c` is the card controller and `stm32-usart.c` the console.

steps.title: The end of the chain
steps.body: `kernel_init()` runs `/sbin/init`. From here on, the boot chain is over and the distribution takes over.
